title: Contents
markdown:
# Contents

Perron is the design system of Mylder, a live map of Copenhagen's public transport: every bus, S-tog, metro and regional train, where it is now, and how sure we are about that. The map is the product. Everything else floats over it on glass and says, in words and in the shape of every dot, how sure we are about what it shows.

## The brand

Mylder is Danish for a swarm or a throng: the city's vehicles, moving all at once. It has one look, in a light and a dark theme.

- **Honest.** Every vehicle shows how fresh its data is, and every sentence says no more than the data knows.
- **Calm.** The map and the vehicles carry the colour. The interface around them is ink, glass and neutral surfaces.
- **Of Copenhagen.** The operators' own line colours, the city's names, Danish and English side by side, the 24-hour clock.

The mark is on [Logos](logos.md), the brand colour on [Semantic colours](semantic-colours.md#brand), and the voice in [Content design](../content-design.md).

## Pages

Each page gives the rules for one foundation, then its tokens or files. The tables are rebuilt from the package's `tokens/`, `icons/` and `logos/` folders by `npm run tokens`, so a page always shows what the build ships. Edit the prose around a table, never the table.

| Page                                      | What it covers                                                        |
| ----------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| [Accessibility](accessibility.md)         | The WCAG 2.2 AA target: what the build enforces, what a person checks |
| [Elevation](elevation.md)                 | The surface ladder, glass and shadows                                 |
| [Icons](icons.md)                         | The icon files, their size scale and style                            |
| [Layout](layout.md)                       | Breakpoints, the map screen, stacking and shared measures             |
| [Logos](logos.md)                         | The Mylder mark and how it is used                                    |
| [Motion](motion.md)                       | Durations, easing and reduced motion                                  |
| [Primitive colours](primitive-colours.md) | The palette every colour token points at                              |
| [Semantic colours](semantic-colours.md)   | Every colour token in both themes                                     |
| [Semantic spacing](semantic-spacing.md)   | Spacing, radius, border widths and the focus ring                     |
| [Typography](typography.md)               | The three families, the sixteen roles, sizes and line heights         |

Two more pages hold what only a live map needs:

| Page                          | What it covers                                       |
| ----------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| [Data states](data-states.md) | The five Prik states, delays and kinds of disruption |
| [Map](map.md)                 | Line widths, dot sizes and dimming on the map canvas |

## Using the tokens

- Install `@mylder/perron` and load `@mylder/perron/perron.css` once at the app root. It brings the fonts, the custom properties for both themes and for reduced motion, the typography classes and a few page defaults.
- Pages name tokens the way the sources do, `color.text.primary`. In CSS that token is `var(--perron-color-text-primary)`: `--perron-`, then the name with dots as hyphens. Never copy a value.
- In script, `@mylder/perron/tokens.ts` has every value per theme, typed by name, and the reduced motion values under `modifiers`.
- Light is the default theme. Set `data-theme="dark"` on any element for dark; without it, the system's dark mode applies. Reduced motion follows the system setting on its own.
- Icons and logos are SVG files in `@mylder/perron/icons/` and `@mylder/perron/logos/`, listed with their use in `icons.json` and `logos.json`.
- A token changes only in Perron's own repository, in `packages/perron/tokens/*.tokens.json`, followed by `npm run tokens`. Never edit a generated file, or a table on these pages, by hand.

title: Accessibility
markdown:
# Accessibility

Perron targets [WCAG 2.2](https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/) level AA. Part of it the build proves on every change: `npm run check` fails when any check below breaks. The rest no build can see, so a person checks it on every screen before it ships.

## What the build checks

- **Text contrast (1.4.3).** Every text colour reaches 4.5:1 on `color.surface.default`, `raised` and `inset`, in both themes. The test lists the deliberate misses by name: `color.text.tertiary` and `color.transit.delay.unknown`, which are only for hints, captions and the "—" of an unknown delay, always next to stronger text. Status and brand text also reach 4.5:1 on their own tinted surfaces.
- **Non-text contrast (1.4.11).** What shows where a control is, or what state something is in, reaches 3:1 against every surface: `color.border.control`, the focus ring and the status fills. Decorative lines, `color.border.subtle` and `color.border.strong`, are exempt, and their descriptions say so.
- **The focus ring (2.4.7, 1.4.11)** reaches 3:1 on every surface and on the map's land, water and parks.
- **The surface ladder.** `color.surface.inset` stands apart from `color.surface.raised` by at least 1.15:1 in both themes, so an inset track reads without a border. See [Elevation](elevation.md#surfaces).
- **Line badges.** Label colours on line colours are measured, and the official pairs that miss are listed. See [Semantic colours](semantic-colours.md#line-colours).
- **Reduced motion (2.3.3, a AAA criterion met anyway)** lives in the tokens: when the system asks for less motion, transitions take 0.01 ms. See [Motion](motion.md).

### Text on surfaces

### The focus ring on the map

<!-- contrast 3: color.border.focus on color.map.land color.map.water color.map.park -->

| -------------------- | ---------- | ----------- | ---------- | --------- | ---------- | --------- |
| `color.border.focus` | 15.48:1    | 11.78:1     | 13.61:1    | 14.88:1   | 16.27:1    | 13.89:1   |

<!-- /contrast -->

## Rules

- **Focus.** Every interactive element shows the ring on `:focus-visible`: a `focus.width` solid outline in `color.border.focus`, `focus.offset` away from the element. `perron.css` sets it for the whole page. Never remove an outline without drawing the ring another way.
- **Targets (2.5.8).** Anything people press is at least `size.target-min` square, or has that much room around it. Perron's controls are larger: the smallest, a small button, is `size.button-sm`.
- **Colour never alone (1.4.1).** A status colour comes with a word or an icon, a data state with its name next to the dot, a line colour with the line's name.
- **Hover (1.4.13).** Anything shown on hover is also reachable by selecting the item, because touch and keyboard users never see hover. A hover card stays while the pointer is over it and closes with Esc.
- **Keys.** Esc closes the topmost thing first: a dialog, then a detail panel, then a highlight. + and − zoom, arrow keys pan.
- **State in words.** Toggles say their state in words as well as in looks ("Follow" / "Following"). One primary action per panel.
- **Moving things.** Loops (the follow blink and the report and selection pulses) stop in their component when the system asks for less motion. The tokens only shorten transitions.

<!-- tokens: focus.* size.target-min -->

| Token             | Value                    | Use                                                                   |
| ----------------- | ------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `focus.width`     | `2px` (border.width.050) | Width of the focus ring                                               |
| `focus.offset`    | `2px`                    | Gap between the focused element and its ring                          |
| `size.target-min` | `24px`                   | Smallest touch or pointer target, from WCAG 2.2 target size (minimum) |

<!-- /tokens -->

## What a person checks

Before a screen ships, check what the build can't:

- **Keyboard.** Every action is reachable in a sensible order. Only an open dialog traps focus, and closing anything returns focus to where it came from.
- **Names.** Every control has an accessible name; an icon button carries a label. The map has a text alternative: the vehicle list.
- **Images.** Images and the mark have alt text, or are hidden from assistive technology when they are decoration.
- **Zoom and reflow (1.4.4, 1.4.10).** At 200% zoom and at 320 px wide, nothing is cut off or overlaps, and only the map scrolls sideways.
- **Text spacing (1.4.12).** Wider line, letter and word spacing breaks nothing.
- **Announcements.** Live updates, such as countdowns and moving vehicles, don't flood a screen reader: a polite live region announces changes of state only.
- **Forced colours.** In Windows' contrast themes, the focus ring and the selected state still show. The Prik shapes keep each data state readable without colour.

title: Elevation
markdown:
# Elevation

The surface and shadow tokens. The map is the ground; everything else floats over it, and depth shows first in the surface colour, then in a shadow.

## Surfaces

- Floating panels are glass: `color.surface.overlay` with a backdrop blur of `effect.glass-blur` and a saturation of `effect.glass-saturate`. On phones, panels full of text use `color.surface.default` instead, so text never sits on moving map.
- Inside a panel, cards and inputs sit on `color.surface.raised`, and tracks, counts and inset boxes on `color.surface.inset`.
- Hover is `color.surface.hover`, laid over whatever is beneath. A selected row is `color.surface.selected`.
- `color.surface.inverse` is the primary button, pressed toggles and the chart's value tip, with `color.text.inverse` on it.

<!-- tokens: color.surface.default color.surface.raised color.surface.inset color.surface.overlay color.surface.hover color.surface.selected color.surface.inverse effect.* -->

| Token                    | Light                           | Dark                            | Use                                                                |
| ------------------------ | ------------------------------- | ------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `color.surface.default`  | `#FAFBF9` (palette.neutral.50)  | `#12181B` (palette.neutral.900) | Opaque panel background; text on inverse surfaces                  |
| `color.surface.raised`   | `#FFFFFF` (palette.neutral.0)   | `#1D2428` (palette.neutral.800) | Inputs, selected segment                                           |
| `color.surface.inset`    | `#EBEEEB` (palette.neutral.100) | `#283237` (palette.neutral.700) | Segmented control track, counts, inset boxes                       |
| `color.surface.overlay`  | `rgba(250, 251, 249, 0.9)`      | `rgba(18, 24, 27, 0.88)`        | Translucent floating panels over the map (used with backdrop blur) |
| `color.surface.hover`    | `rgba(18, 24, 27, 0.05)`        | `rgba(235, 238, 235, 0.06)`     | Hover state layer                                                  |
| `color.surface.selected` | `rgba(18, 24, 27, 0.09)`        | `rgba(235, 238, 235, 0.09)`     | Selected row                                                       |
| `color.surface.inverse`  | `#12181B` (color.text.primary)  | `#EBEEEB` (color.text.primary)  | Primary buttons, pressed icon buttons, chart tooltip               |
| `effect.glass-blur`      | `16px`                          | `16px`                          | Backdrop blur behind glass panels                                  |
| `effect.glass-saturate`  | `1.3`                           | `1.3`                           | Backdrop saturation behind glass panels                            |

<!-- /tokens -->

Inset stands apart from raised in both themes, so a track reads without a border: a step darker in light, a step lighter in dark. The build keeps the two at least 1.15:1 apart.

<!-- contrast 1.15: color.surface.inset on color.surface.raised -->

| Colour                | Light raised | Dark raised |
| --------------------- | ------------ | ----------- |
| `color.surface.inset` | 1.17:1       | 1.20:1      |

<!-- /contrast -->

## Shadows

Floating panels carry `shadow.panel`. Nothing else casts a shadow, except the selected segment of a segmented control, with `shadow.thumb`. Both are set per theme: a dark surface needs a darker, wider shadow to show at all.

<!-- tokens: shadow.* -->

| Token          | Light                                                                             | Dark                                                                         | Use                                     |
| -------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------- |
| `shadow.panel` | `0px 1px 2px 0px rgba(18, 24, 27, 0.06), 0px 10px 30px 0px rgba(18, 24, 27, 0.1)` | `0px 1px 2px 0px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.35), 0px 14px 36px 0px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.38)` | Floating panels                         |
| `shadow.thumb` | `0px 1px 2px 0px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.14)`                                             | `0px 1px 2px 0px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.4)`                                         | Selected segment in a segmented control |

<!-- /tokens -->

Stacking order is on [Layout](layout.md#stacking).

title: Icons
markdown: # Icons One small set, drawn for Mylder. Perron draws its own stroke icons rather than use an icon font or a third-party set: there are few of them, each drawn on a grid near the size it shows at. The files are in `packages/perron/icons/`, and `icons.json` there lists them by category with the size and use of each. ## Sizes Every icon renders at one of three steps, set with `--perron-icon-size` (one of the tokens below) and never with a raw width. Each icon is drawn on the grid closest to its step, so its stroke stays between 1.5 and 1.8 px. A larger icon is a new drawing, not a scaled one. | Token | Value | Use | | --------------- | ------ | -------------------------------------------------------- | | `icon.size.325` | `13px` | Inline with label and caption text: the disruption icons | | `icon.size.400` | `16px` | Inside controls: search, zoom, locate, close | | `icon.size.450` | `18px` | Top bar buttons: kiosk mode, about | ## Style - Strokes with round caps and joins, 1.5 to 1.8 px on the icon's own grid. Fills only for a dot, such as the point of the info icon. - Drawn in `currentColor`, so an icon takes the colour of the text around it. Set the colour on the text, never on the icon. - The `.perron-icon` class in `perron.css` sizes an inline SVG icon from `--perron-icon-size`, and keeps it from shrinking in a flex row. - An icon sits next to a word or inside a labelled button; it never carries meaning alone. Next to text it is hidden from screen readers (`aria-hidden="true"`). Alone, it needs an accessible name. - No icon font, no emoji, no third-party icon set. A new icon follows this page, joins `icons.json`, and the check confirms its grid, stroke and colour. ## The set ### Map | Icon | Name | Grid | Size | Use | | --------------------------------------------------------- | -------- | ----- | ---------------------- | ----------------------------- | | | `plus` | 16 px | `icon.size.400`, 16 px | Zoom in | | | `minus` | 16 px | `icon.size.400`, 16 px | Zoom out | | | `locate` | 16 px | `icon.size.400`, 16 px | Centre the map on the network | ### Actions | Icon | Name | Grid | Size | Use | | --------------------------------------------------------- | -------- | ----- | ---------------------- | -------------------------------------- | | | `search` | 16 px | `icon.size.400`, 16 px | The search field | | | `close` | 16 px | `icon.size.400`, 16 px | Close a panel, a dialog or a highlight | ### App | Icon | Name | Grid | Size | Use | | ---------------------------------------------------------- | --------- | ----- | ---------------------- | -------------- | | | `monitor` | 18 px | `icon.size.450`, 18 px | Kiosk mode | | | `info` | 18 px | `icon.size.450`, 18 px | About and help | ### Disruptions | Icon | Name | Grid | Size | Use | | ------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------ | ----- | ---------------------- | ------------------ | | | `warning` | 14 px | `icon.size.325`, 13 px | Delays | | | `signal-off` | 14 px | `icon.size.325`, 13 px | Data feed problems | | | `diversion` | 14 px | `icon.size.325`, 13 px | Diversions | | | `calendar` | 14 px | `icon.size.325`, 13 px | Planned works |

title: Layout
markdown:
# Layout

Where the layout switches, and what the map screen is built from.

## Breakpoints

Each breakpoint is the width below which the screen changes.

- Under `breakpoint.desktop`, the filters that are coming later go.
- Under `breakpoint.tablet`, the city name, the date and the legend go.
- Under `breakpoint.phone`, the sheet and the detail panel become bottom sheets, and the top bar shrinks to `size.top-bar-phone`.
- Under `breakpoint.compact-phone`, the brand mark goes.

<!-- tokens: breakpoint.* -->

| Token                      | Value    | Use                            |
| -------------------------- | -------- | ------------------------------ |
| `breakpoint.compact-phone` | `380px`  | Hide the brand mark            |
| `breakpoint.phone`         | `760px`  | Bottom sheets, compact top bar |
| `breakpoint.tablet`        | `1180px` | Hide city name, day and legend |
| `breakpoint.desktop`       | `1400px` | Hide "Later" chips             |

<!-- /tokens -->

## Page shell

The map fills the screen, and the page shell floats over it.

- A top bar of glass groups runs along the top: brand, clock, filters and settings.
- The overview sheet sits on the left and the detail panel on the right.
- Map controls and the scale sit at the bottom right, and the legend at the bottom centre.
- Panels keep `size.panel-gap` from the screen edge and from each other.

<!-- tokens: size.top-bar size.top-bar-phone size.sheet-width size.detail-width size.sheet-peek size.panel-gap -->

| Token                | Value   | Use                                                                  |
| -------------------- | ------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `size.top-bar`       | `46px`  | Top bar group height (42 on phones)                                  |
| `size.top-bar-phone` | `42px`  | Height of a top bar group on phones                                  |
| `size.sheet-width`   | `376px` | Overview sheet width on desktop                                      |
| `size.detail-width`  | `364px` | Detail panel width on desktop                                        |
| `size.sheet-peek`    | `182px` | Bottom sheet height when closed on phones                            |
| `size.panel-gap`     | `12px`  | Distance between floating panels and the viewport edge (8 on phones) |

<!-- /tokens -->

## Stacking

From lowest to highest: map controls, the overview sheet, the highlight chip, the detail panel, the top bar, the tooltip, then a dialog over a `color.scrim` backdrop.

<!-- tokens: z-index.* color.scrim -->

| Token                  | Value                    | Use                                               |
| ---------------------- | ------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------- |
| `z-index.map-controls` | `3`                      | Legend, map controls, scale, attribution          |
| `z-index.sheet`        | `4`                      | Overview sheet, kiosk bar                         |
| `z-index.highlight`    | `5`                      | Highlight chip                                    |
| `z-index.detail`       | `6`                      | Detail panel                                      |
| `z-index.top-bar`      | `7`                      | Brand, filters and clock along the top of the map |
| `z-index.tooltip`      | `8`                      | Map hover card, above every panel                 |
| `z-index.dialog`       | `10`                     | Modal dialog over everything                      |
| `color.scrim`          | `rgba(10, 14, 16, 0.42)` | Backdrop behind modal dialogs                     |

<!-- /tokens -->

## Other layout properties

A measure lives here when two places must agree on it, such as a component and the list that virtualises its rows. A measure only one component's CSS reads stays in that CSS.

<!-- tokens: size.control size.button size.button-sm size.input size.segment size.badge size.badge-lg size.vehicle-row size.target-min -->

title: Logos
markdown: # Logos The Mylder mark, and how it is used. The files are in `packages/perron/logos/`, and `logos.json` there lists them with the ground each is drawn for. ## The mark The mark is a bus dot, an S-tog dot and an estimated ring: three of the ways a vehicle can look on the map. Its colours are tokens, each in its theme's value: the bus dot is `color.transit.mode.bus`, the S-tog dot line A's `color.transit.line.a`, the ring `color.text.primary`. A file is an image and can't follow the theme, so there is one file per theme, and the check holds each file's colours to its theme's tokens. | Token | Light | Dark | Use | | ------------------------ | ------------------------------- | ------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------- | | `color.transit.mode.bus` | `#D99A00` (palette.yellow.500) | `#F2B630` (palette.yellow.300) | All bus lines | | `color.transit.line.a` | `#00A1DE` | `#00A1DE` | S-tog A | | `color.text.primary` | `#12181B` (palette.neutral.900) | `#EBEEEB` (palette.neutral.100) | Main text and icons; also the focus ring | ## Usage - Keep the mark as drawn: its three shapes and colours are data states, so a recoloured, outlined or rearranged mark says something else. - Set it beside the wordmark: "mylder" in lowercase, in `typography.heading-md` set bold. The mark alone stands in only where space is tight, such as an app icon. - Keep clear space of at least the ring's width around it, and set it no smaller than its drawn size, 27 × 19 px. - Use the file drawn for the ground it sits on: `mylder-mark.svg` on light, `mylder-mark-dark.svg` on dark. ## Files ### Brand | Logo | File | Theme | Use | | ------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------- | ----- | ---------------- | | | `logos/mylder-mark.svg` | Light | On light grounds | | | `logos/mylder-mark-dark.svg` | Dark | On dark grounds |

title: Motion
markdown:
# Motion

Motion explains a change of place. The sheet slides, the camera eases to a selection, and meters ease to new values. Vehicles glide between reports instead of jumping.

## Durations

- **Transitions** move something from one place or value to another, once: `duration.sheet`, `duration.meter`, `duration.camera` and `duration.follow`.
- **Loops** repeat while something is true. A new report pulses once around its vehicle (`duration.report-pulse`), a ring pulses around the selected vehicle (`duration.selection-pulse`), and the follow indicator blinks while the camera follows (`duration.blink`).

<!-- tokens: duration.* -->

| Token                      | Value    | Reduced motion | Use                                                   |
| -------------------------- | -------- | -------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| `duration.sheet`           | `320ms`  | `0.01ms`       | Bottom sheet open and close                           |
| `duration.meter`           | `800ms`  | `0.01ms`       | Meter fill change                                     |
| `duration.camera`          | `750ms`  | `0.01ms`       | Map camera fly-to                                     |
| `duration.follow`          | `500ms`  | `0.01ms`       | Camera fly-to when following starts                   |
| `duration.blink`           | `1400ms` |                | Recording dot blink while following                   |
| `duration.report-pulse`    | `1100ms` |                | Ring that expands when a vehicle reports its position |
| `duration.selection-pulse` | `1600ms` |                | Ring around the selected vehicle                      |

<!-- /tokens -->

## Easing

The sheet has its own curve, which settles slowly so a long slide doesn't stop abruptly. Everything else eases with `easing.standard`, the browser's `ease`.

<!-- tokens: easing.* -->

| Token             | Value                              | Use               |
| ----------------- | ---------------------------------- | ----------------- |
| `easing.sheet`    | `cubic-bezier(0.2, 0.8, 0.2, 1)`   | Bottom sheet      |
| `easing.standard` | `cubic-bezier(0.25, 0.1, 0.25, 1)` | CSS ease (meters) |

<!-- /tokens -->

## Reduced motion

When the system asks for less motion, the transition tokens take 0.01 ms: their values under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` are in the table's Reduced motion column. The value is 0.01 ms rather than 0, so `transitionend` and animation events still fire. CSS that reads the tokens needs nothing more.

- **Loops** keep their durations in the tokens, because a loop at 0.01 ms would flicker. Each component that runs a loop stops it under reduced motion.
- Vehicles move to each new report without gliding.

The values come from the resolver's `motion` modifier. Its default context, `full`, is empty, because base already holds the full-motion values; its `reduced` context points at `packages/perron/tokens/motion-reduced.tokens.json`. The build writes the overrides into each output:

| Output               | Reduced motion                                                             |
| -------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `tokens.css`         | The overrides inside `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)`, on `:root` |
| `tokens.ts`          | `modifiers.motion.reduced`, as CSS text and as numbers                     |
| `penpot.tokens.json` | A `motion-reduced` set, and a Motion group with Full and Reduced themes    |

## Timings in script

Script that animates, such as the map camera's fly-to, reads `numeric` from `tokens.ts`, and `modifiers.motion.reduced.numeric` when `matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)')` matches. Both hold durations in milliseconds.

# Primitive colours

The palette holds Perron's raw colour values. Every `color` token points at a palette step in each theme, so retuning a step moves every colour built on it. Components and apps never read the palette: they use the `color` tokens on [Semantic colours](semantic-colours.md), and a new need gets a new `color` token, never a palette value.

## Steps

A neutral ramp runs from `0` (white) to `950`. Five hues, blue, green, orange, red and yellow, have five steps each. Steps rise as the colour darkens, and each hue step has one job:

- **100**: light-theme tint.
- **300**: dark-theme fill and text.
- **500**: light-theme fill.
- **700**: light-theme text, 4.5:1 on every light surface.
- **900**: dark-theme tint.

Gaps in the neutral ramp are room for new steps. A translucent colour is written in full on its `color` token, with a palette step's components plus an alpha, and a test checks its RGB is a palette step.

# Semantic colours

Every colour token in both themes. A `color` token says what a colour is for and points at a [primitive colour](primitive-colours.md) in each theme.

## Light and dark

- Light is the default theme. Dark comes from `data-theme="dark"` on any element or, without an explicit theme, from the system's dark mode. `data-theme="light"` keeps an element light inside a dark page, so one page can show both themes side by side.
- Both themes define the same names, and the build fails when one is missing.
- Dark colours are their own palette steps, chosen for the dark surfaces, not an inversion of the light ones: 300 for status and brand fills and text, 900 for tints, the light neutrals for text.
- Base tokens never point at a theme token. A custom property resolves where it is declared, so a base token built from a theme colour would keep the root theme's value inside a nested `data-theme`.

## Text

- Three text colours for the interface. Use `color.text.primary` for what people read first, and `color.text.secondary` for supporting text. Keep `color.text.tertiary` for hints, axis labels and captions next to stronger text: it misses 4.5:1 on purpose (the figures are on [Accessibility](accessibility.md)), so set sentences people must read in primary or secondary.
- `color.text.inverse` sits on `color.surface.inverse`, the primary button and pressed toggles.
- On a coloured fill, text is `color.text.on-color.dark` or `color.text.on-color.light`, whichever the fill was paired with.

## Space

Every padding, margin and gap comes from the spacing scale: nine steps from 2 to 32 px on a 4 px base. The number divided by 100 is the count of 4 px units, so `space.300` is 12 px.

- Parts of a detail panel sit 12 px apart (`space.300`), and blocks of a pane 24 px apart (`space.600`).

title: Typography
markdown:
# Typography

Three families, self-hosted. Familjen Grotesk is for headings and the wordmark, Schibsted Grotesk for text and labels, and JetBrains Mono for data. Fonts load from this package, never from Google Fonts, which would send visitors' IP addresses to Google.

## Roles

Sixteen roles, one per job. Set every piece of text with a role, either as a class (`perron-typography-body`) or as a composite custom property (`font: var(--perron-typography-body)` plus `letter-spacing: var(--perron-typography-body-tracking)`).

- Anything people compare down a column is a `data` role: times, countdowns, counts, delays, percentages. They use tabular figures, so columns line up.
- `overline` sets its text in capitals: the class adds `text-transform: uppercase`, and with the custom property you add it yourself. Write the source text in sentence case.
- On phones, `display` and `data-xl` step down to `font.size.800`, and `stat` to `font.size.600`. These are the only places a component reaches for a size directly.

title: Data states
markdown:
# Data states

Every vehicle is a Prik, drawn in its line colour in one of five states. The shapes are the system's signature: never reuse a ring or a dashed ring to mean anything else, and never draw a vehicle without its state.

| State          | Shape         | Means                                                  |
| -------------- | ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| Live           | A solid dot   | A GPS report under a minute old                        |
| Ageing         | A fainter dot | A report 1 to 5 minutes old                            |
| Estimated      | A ring        | Placed from the timetable and the latest delay         |
| Timetable only | A dashed ring | No real-time data at all                               |
| No signal      | A grey dot    | Silent for over 5 minutes, left where it was last seen |

- Always write the state in words next to the dot. Legends list all five states, in this order, even when one has no vehicles.
- `color.data-state.no-signal` means a vehicle has gone silent. Use it for that alone.
- On the map, draw dots on a canvas, with a halo of `color.data-state.halo` and, for light line colours on the light map, a hairline of `color.data-state.outline`.

## Geometry

The `prik` tokens give the geometry of each shape at any size: insets, stroke widths, the dash, and the age thresholds between live, ageing and no signal.

| `prik.ageing-threshold`       | `300000ms`    | Reports younger than this (and at least live-threshold old) are ageing; older is no signal |

title: Content design
markdown:
# Content design

How every word in Mylder reads: plain sentences, exact about certainty, in English, Danish, Swedish and Norwegian Bokmål. The foundations are in [foundations/](foundations/README.md).

- Say what is happening in plain sentences, then how sure we are. "Signal fault at Danshøj. Trains between Flintholm and Ny Ellebjerg run slower than planned." Never claim more certainty than the data has: a vehicle without a signal is "No signal since 08:02", not a guess.
- Sentence case everywhere: "Show whole line", "Back to the map", "Reporting live, by operator". Capitals come only from the `perron-typography-overline` style, so write the source text in sentence case.
- Speak about the city and its vehicles, not about the person. Address them only in instructions: "Try a line number such as 5C."
- Numbers: 24-hour clock ("08:14"), a space before units ("4 min", "45 km/h"), the true minus sign for early ("−1"), "—" for unknown, "≈" before estimates, "~" before estimated times. Countdowns under 45 seconds read "Now".
- Data states and delays always use the words in the table below, in every language, so every screen agrees.
- Name keys in help text: "Keys: + and − zoom, arrows pan, Esc closes panels."
- No emoji, no exclamation marks.

## Data-state and delay words

Components take these from the locale dictionaries in `packages/perron/src/locale/`, which a test holds to this table. Change a word in both.

| English          | Danish        | Swedish          | Norwegian Bokmål |
| ---------------- | ------------- | ---------------- | ---------------- |
| Live             | Live          | Live             | Live             |
| Ageing           | Ældre         | Äldre            | Eldre            |
| Estimated        | Beregnet      | Beräknad         | Beregnet         |
| Timetable only   | Kun køreplan  | Endast tidtabell | Kun rutetabell   |
| No signal        | Intet signal  | Ingen signal     | Ingen signal     |
| Delays           | Forsinkelser  | Förseningar      | Forsinkelser     |
| Running normally | Kører normalt | Går som vanligt  | Går som normalt  |
| Show on map      | Vis på kort   | Visa på kartan   | Vis på kartet    |

title: Glossary
markdown:
# Glossary

The words used to talk about Perron, Mylder's design system. The words Mylder shows its riders are in [content-design.md](content-design.md).

## Layers

**Component**:
A reusable piece of interface built on Base UI, with MUI-shaped props and no knowledge of transit.
_Avoid_: Widget, primitive

**Pattern**:
A piece of a Mylder screen built only from components, which takes Mylder's domain data as props, such as a departure row.
_Avoid_: Composition, template, organism

## Building a component

**Contract**:
The rules every component follows: its props, events, styling, files and checks.
_Avoid_: Guidelines, conventions

**Spec**:
What a piece of work must do, written before it is built. A component's spec is its page in `docs/components/`: its anatomy, Base UI parts, props, tokens, keyboard behaviour and owned strings. Any other spec, such as one for a roadmap phase, is a GitHub issue.
_Avoid_: Brief, design doc

**Ticket**:
One sub-issue of a spec's issue: a slice of the work that can be built and checked on its own, naming the tickets that block it.
_Avoid_: Task, story

**Read-back**:
The machine-readable copy of a component's Penpot design, `penpot/<name>.json`, that code and checks are compared against.
_Avoid_: Export, snapshot

**Code map**:
The file that pairs each Penpot variant property and layer of a component with a React prop or CSS state.
_Avoid_: Mapping, Code Connect

**Gate**:
A point a component may not pass until a check or a person says yes.
_Avoid_: Step, checkpoint

**Pre-flight**:
The files a skill must read before it may write anything.
_Avoid_: Setup, context

**Owned string**:
A word a component shows or announces on its own, rather than one the caller passes, such as "Close". It comes from the locale dictionaries.
_Avoid_: Internal label, default text

**Intent**:
A value of a component's `color` prop, backed by tokens: what the colour means, not which colour it is.
_Avoid_: Tone, colour name

## The factory

**Factory**:
The local system of Claude Code runs that moves each component through the loop, from its issue to a ready PR.
_Avoid_: Pipeline, bot

**Run**:
One start of the factory on one component, from the moment it claims the issue to the next gate, cap or ready PR. It remembers only what the issue, the PR and `pipeline.yaml` hold.
_Avoid_: Session, job

**Scorecard**:
What one stage run records about itself in `pipeline.yaml`: its attempts, the checks that failed, its pre-flight reads, its review findings, its questions and its cost.
_Avoid_: Metrics, report

**Scorer**:
A rubric that a fresh-context agent applies to the transcripts of runs, giving each a pass, a fail or insufficient evidence, with a reason.
_Avoid_: Judge, eval, grader

**Touch**:
Anything the maintainer does for a component beyond the two gates: answering a `[PENDING]` question, clearing `needs-human`, sending a design back, asking for changes on the PR or pushing a commit to it.
_Avoid_: Steer, intervention

**Retro**:
The run that improves the factory itself. After every fifth merged component, it scores those runs and opens one PR to the instructions behind their failures.
_Avoid_: Self-improvement agent, outer loop

**Replay**:
One stage run again on a merged component's frozen inputs, to compare a proposed change with what it replaces.
_Avoid_: Shadow run, benchmark
